headline_marked: HSC and equivalent exam results [[to be published]] on Saturday
headline: HSC and equivalent exam results to be published on Saturday
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations at 11am on Saturday. Candidates can check their results at institutions, online or via SMS.
details: The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are scheduled for release on Saturday. Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce them at 11am.

Candidates will be able to check their results at their respective institutions, online, or by sending an SMS from any mobile phone number. The results will be available on the education boards’ websites, including https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd.

To check results via SMS, students need to type HSC, followed by a space, the three-letter abbreviation of their education board, another space, their roll number, and the examination year. This message must be sent to 16140. For example: HSC DHA 123456 2026.
Institutions can download the results by navigating to the results section of the website and entering their board name and Educational Institution Identification Number (EIIN).

Applications for script scrutiny and re-evaluation will be accepted online from November 1 to November 7. Further instructions and the application process details are available on the education boards’ websites.

To check results via SMS, students need to type HSC, followed by a space, the three-letter abbreviation of their education board, another space, their roll number, and the examination year. This message must be sent to 16140. For example: HSC DHA 123456 2026.

Institutions can download the results by navigating to the results section of the website and entering their board name and Educational Institution Identification Number (EIIN).

Applications for script scrutiny and re-evaluation will be accepted online from November 1 to November 7. Further instructions and the application process details are available on the education boards’ websites.

headline_marked: Former Air Force officer [[Tahsif Souri jumps into Turag River]] while fleeing alleged uniformed men
headline: Former Air Force officer Tahsif Souri jumps into Turag River while fleeing alleged uniformed men
summary: Tahsif Souri's friend Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip claims they were chased by unidentified men in uniform before Tahsif jumped into the Turag River. The PBI is investigating the incident.
details: Former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri allegedly jumped into the Turag River on October 27 after being chased by several people, his friend Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip told investigators. Dip, who was taken into custody for questioning, claimed the individuals were wearing uniforms. The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) is continuing its investigation, not yet fully convinced by Dip's account.

According to Dip's statement, he and Tahsif were at Mazar Basti near the Turag River on the night of the incident. Dip stated that while they were talking, they were suddenly chased by several people. Tahsif then jumped into the river, while Dip managed to escape. PBI investigators visited the scene with Dip, who recounted the events near boundary pillar 29 of the Turag River in Tongi.

Investigators recovered a motorcycle from the area, which is being verified if it belonged to Tahsif. A local tea stall owner reported seeing the motorcycle parked for two days before police took it away and later returned it. Tahsif's body was recovered from the Rajabari ferry terminal area on October 28, a day after his disappearance.

CCTV footage showed Tahsif with Dip shortly before he went missing. Tahsif's family identified Dip as a junior friend. Tahsif's father is demanding a fair investigation into his son's death. The PBI is conducting a parallel investigation with the River Police.
